pre: Finish the guided photo walkthrough in the Photos tab before you touch anything. Harnesses, hoses, brackets and belt routing are what people forget.
Negative terminal first. Tuck the cable away from the post.
Pull the fuel pump fuse or relay and crank until the engine stalls, or use the service port if fitted. Wear eye protection and keep ignition sources away.
Catch fluids in sealed containers and take them to a recycler. Coolant is toxic to pets.
Refrigerant must be recovered by a certified shop. Never vent it.
post: Check nothing still ties the engine to the car
Walk around it. Look for forgotten ground straps, wire clips, hoses and the fuel line. Tag any loose connector.
Use a rated hoist and leveler. Take up weight slowly, check for snags at every inch, and never put any part of your body under the load.
Mount it on a stand and bag the hardware
Bag bolts by location and write on the bag. Match each bag to a photo.

engines.name: GM LS1 5.7L
steps: Remove intake tube, airbox and MAF
Unplug the MAF and IAT sensors. Photograph the vacuum and PCV lines before pulling them.
Remove accessories
Release the belt tensioner, mark the belt path, then unbolt the alternator, power steering pump and A/C compressor. Tie them aside without opening lines.
Disconnect the engine harness
Label every connector. Check the knock sensors, injectors, coils, cam and crank sensors and the oil pressure sender.
Disconnect cooling and heater hoses
Photograph hose routing. Remove the upper and lower radiator hoses and both heater hoses.
Unbolt the exhaust
Separate manifolds or headers from the downpipes. Spray penetrating oil on seized studs first.
Separate the transmission
Support the transmission. Remove the bellhousing bolts and, on automatics, the torque converter bolts through the inspection cover.
Unbolt the motor mounts
Support the engine with the hoist before removing the mount bolts.

engines.name: Honda B-series (B16/B18)
steps: Remove intake and airbox
Unplug the MAP, IAT and throttle position connectors. Photograph vacuum lines.
Disconnect the harness at the firewall and ECU side
Label the engine harness connectors and the ground straps on the block and chassis.
Remove the radiator and hoses
Photograph fan wiring. Disconnect the heater hoses at the firewall.
Remove the axles from the transmission
Unbolt the lower ball joints or knuckle, then pry the axles out of the transmission. Plug the openings.
Disconnect shift linkage and clutch line
Photograph the cable positions. Cap the hydraulic line.
Remove accessories as needed
Release belt tension and unbolt the A/C compressor and power steering pump. Tie them aside.
Unbolt the exhaust and mounts
Separate the header from the downpipe. Support the engine and transmission before removing the mounts. These usually lift out together.

engines.name: Toyota 2JZ-GE 3.0L
steps: Remove intake plumbing and throttle body
Unplug the MAF, IAT and throttle sensors. Photograph the vacuum map before removing hoses.
Disconnect the engine harness
Label every connector and ground. Mark injector and coil plugs by cylinder.
Remove the radiator and fan shroud
Photograph hose routing. Remove the heater hoses.
Remove accessories
Mark the belt path, then unbolt the alternator, power steering pump and A/C compressor.
Unbolt the exhaust manifold and downpipe
Penetrating oil on the studs first. Expect rusted fasteners.
Disconnect the clutch or transmission and driveshaft
Mark the driveshaft flange. Support the transmission and remove the bellhousing bolts.
Unbolt the motor mounts
Support the engine with the hoist before removing the mount bolts.

engines.name: Chevy Small Block 350
steps: Remove the air cleaner and carburetor or throttle body
Photograph throttle and kickdown linkage and every vacuum line. Cap the fuel line.
Mark the distributor
Mark the rotor position and the housing before removal so you can reinstall at the same timing.
Remove the radiator and fan
Disconnect hoses and transmission cooler lines if fitted. Cap the lines.
Remove accessories
Mark belt routing, then unbolt the alternator, power steering pump and A/C compressor.
Unbolt the exhaust manifolds or headers
Separate from the downpipes. Spray penetrating oil on the bolts first.
Separate the transmission
Support it, remove the bellhousing bolts and on automatics the flexplate-to-converter bolts.
Unbolt the motor mounts
Support the engine with the hoist before removing the mount bolts.
